Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

at North Quay station tomorrow morning. The tickets are for a journey from North Quay to Alderwick on the seventeenth of June, and the return trip is booked for the twentieth. I am not asking the desk to change the dates yet. I want the clerk to check whether the tickets can be exchanged for a later departure because my father has a clinic appointment that may run longer than expected. I will bring the original booking email on my phone and the printed receipt from the kiosk.

The outbound train is the 8:42 service, and the return train is the 16:10 service. Both tickets show coach C and seats 18 and 19. The booking reference is QN 438 271, and the total fare was 64 pounds, paid with my debit card. The receipt has the last four card digits 6038, and the ticket envelopes have my surname written on the front. I checked the journey details last night, and both stations are printed correctly. The appointment is on the same day as the outbound trip, so the possible change concerns the journey after the appointment.

I am returning the tickets together because they were bought as one booking, and I do not know whether the exchange desk needs both originals for a change to only one leg. The printed conditions mention an exchange fee, but they do not give the amount on my receipt. The counter staff may need to confirm whether the fee applies separately to each ticket or once for the booking. I have not been told that an exchange is available, and I have not chosen a replacement train. If the later fare is higher than the amount already paid, please ask me before processing anything because I need to check my budget.

I expect to arrive at North Quay around 9:15 after the morning bus from Elm Road. The bus stop is beside the station entrance, and the walk to the exchange desk takes about five minutes. If the queue is long, I can wait until after I have spoken to my father by phone. His appointment is at 10:30, and the clinic reception said the visit could take between forty minutes and two hours. I have written the clinic number on the back of the receipt, but I will keep the receipt dry and readable. The weather forecast mentions rain, so both tickets are in a clear sleeve inside my blue folder.

The checklist starts:
1. Bring the two original tickets and the printed receipt.
2. Show the booking email if the clerk asks for the reference number.
3. Explain that the appointment may run late and that a later return departure might be needed.
4. Ask about the exchange fee and any fare difference before selecting a train.
5. Keep the receipt and any written information together in the folder.

These are reminders for my visit and not a request to cancel the whole booking. The outbound ticket still relates to the planned clinic journey, and I have not asked anyone to reserve a seat on another service.

When I called the station information line on Monday, a recorded message said that ticket exchanges are handled at the staffed counter. The person who answered could not tell me which later trains would have seats together and said I should bring the originals. I wrote down that information at 4:20 in the afternoon. I did not give the booking reference during the call, and no exchange was started. The staff member also said that the opening hours can change on public holidays. Tomorrow is an ordinary weekday, but I will look for the hours sign near the counter before joining the queue.

My father, David Moran, will travel with me if the clinic visit finishes in time. He is carrying his appointment letter and a small black walking stick, and he prefers an aisle seat because his knee gets stiff after sitting for a long time. The current seats are next to each other according to the booking email. If a later service is offered, please tell me whether two adjacent seats are available before any change is processed. I can consider seats in a different coach, but I do not want to separate our tickets without discussing it first.

I have placed the tickets, receipt, appointment letter copy, and my notes in separate pockets of the folder. The appointment letter copy includes the clinic address, but it has my father's date of birth on it, so I will only show it if it is needed to explain the timing. I will carry my bank card, although I understand that a fee or fare difference may need to be paid at the desk. The original card is in my wallet, and the booking email is saved for offline viewing in case the station signal is weak.

I wrote the journey times on a small card as well as keeping them on my phone because the battery has been unreliable this week. The phone charger is in my bag, and the card says North Quay to Alderwick on June seventeenth, return to North Quay on June twentieth, booking QN 438 271. I will compare any information given at the counter with those details before deciding what to do. If the clerk needs to keep the tickets while checking the fare, please ask how long the check is expected to take and whether I should remain nearby.

I am returning the tickets to the exchange desk tomorrow so the clerk can check the options for the return journey after the clinic appointment. I will listen to the explanation, ask about the fee and any difference in fare, and decide only after I have heard the available choices. If the appointment finishes early, the original 16:10 train may still be suitable, and I have not ruled it out. If it runs late, I may need a later service, but that depends on the appointment and on the ticket conditions. I will take the folder home with me and keep the booking records together while I wait to learn what choices are available."}]
